Let  
\[
u=\frac{a+b}{2},\quad v=\frac{c+d}{2},\quad p=\frac{a-b}{2},\quad q=\frac{c-d}{2}.
\]
Then \(p,q\ge 0\), \(u+v=\frac92\), and \(b\ge c\) gives
\[
p+q\le u-v=:s.
\]
Also,
\[
u^2+v^2+p^2+q^2=\frac{21}{2}.
\]
Since
\[
u^2+v^2=\frac{(u+v)^2+(u-v)^2}{2}
=\frac{81/4+s^2}{2}
=\frac{81}{8}+\frac{s^2}{2},
\]
we get
\[
p^2+q^2=\frac{21}{2}-\frac{81}{8}-\frac{s^2}{2}
=\frac{3-4s^2}{8}.
\]
Because \(p,q\ge0\), \(p+q\ge \sqrt{p^2+q^2}\). Thus
\[
\sqrt{\frac{3-4s^2}{8}}\le p+q\le s,
\]
so
\[
\frac{3-4s^2}{8}\le s^2 \implies s\ge \frac12.
\]

Now
\[
ab-cd=(u^2-p^2)-(v^2-q^2)
=\frac92s-p^2+q^2.
\]
Using \(p^2+q^2=\frac{3-4s^2}{8}\),
\[
ab-cd=\frac92s-\frac{3-4s^2}{8}+2q^2
=-\frac38+\frac92s+\frac12s^2+2q^2.
\]
Since \(s\ge \frac12\) and \(q^2\ge0\),
\[
ab-cd\ge -\frac38+\frac92\cdot\frac12+\frac12\cdot\frac14=2.
\]
Equality occurs at \(s=\frac12,\ q=0,\ p=\frac12\), giving \((a,b,c,d)=(3,2,2,2)\), which satisfies the ordering.

\[
\boxed{2}
\]
